1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Caliper against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) on five public repos with their dependencies installed.
3	
4	`setup` fetches each repo at its pinned commit, installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile
5	(lifecycle scripts off, caches under the corpora directory), and prunes tests, stories and demos from the source
6	directory. `run` dumps RDT once per corpus (scripts/parity-rdt.mjs, cached by commit), runs Caliper in RDT's format
7	with and without --load-dependencies, and reports per corpus:
8	
9	  - components RDT reports (with props) that Caliper also reports, by file and name;
10	  - RDT props not declared by @types/react that Caliper reports;
11	  - shared props whose type text is identical, identical after cosmetic normalization, or gives the same Storybook
12	    control;
13	  - shared props per loss pattern: Caliper's type carrying less than RDT's (a member read left as `X["k"]`, a lost
14	    rest parameter, ...), and two patterns where RDT carries less;
15	  - best-of-N wall time and peak RSS of `extract --json`, without and with --load-dependencies, next to RDT's.
16	
17	--check against --baseline fails when coverage, agreement or same-control rates drop, a loss pattern grows, or BIN is
18	more than 1.1x slower than --base-bin (timed interleaved on the same machine).
19	
20	`oracle` compares Caliper's canonical prop types with TypeScript 7.1's checker on the same corpora and the repo's
21	fixtures (apps/validate/src/oracle.ts), one verdict per shared prop: identical, spelled differently, less precise,
22	wrong, or no checker type. Its --check fails when agreement falls or wrong verdicts rise. It is test-only.
23	
24	docs/parity.md explains the measures.
25	
26	Usage: scripts/parity.py setup [--corpora DIR] [--corpus NAME]... [--install-node-dir DIR]
27	       scripts/parity.py run --bin BIN [--base-bin BIN] [--corpora DIR] [--rdt-dir DIR] [--corpus NAME]...
28	                             [--runs N] [--no-timing] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--baseline FILE] [--check]
29	       scripts/parity.py oracle --bin BIN [--corpora DIR] [--corpus NAME | fixtures]... [--work DIR] [--out FILE]
30	                                [--markdown FILE] [--baseline FILE] [--check]
31	"""
32	import argparse
33	import functools
34	import json
35	import os
36	import re
37	import shutil
38	import subprocess
39	import sys
40	import time
41	
42	ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
43	
44	CORPORA = [
45	    {
46	        'name': 'mantine',
47	        'repo': 'mantinedev/mantine',
48	        'commit': 'e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d',
49	        'clone': 'mantine',
50	        'src': 'packages/@mantine/core/src',
51	        'manager': 'yarn',
52	    },
53	    {
54	        'name': 'chakra',
55	        'repo': 'chakra-ui/chakra-ui',
56	        'commit': 'fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9',
57	        'clone': 'chakra-ui',
58	        'src': 'packages/react/src',
59	        'manager': 'pnpm',
60	    },
61	    {
62	        'name': 'shadcn',
63	        'repo': 'shadcn-ui/ui',
64	        'commit': 'ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b',
65	        'clone': 'shadcn-ui',
66	        'src': 'apps/v4',
67	        'manager': 'pnpm',
68	    },
69	    {
70	        'name': 'antd',
71	        'repo': 'ant-design/ant-design',
72	        'commit': 'ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538',
73	        'clone': 'ant-design',
74	        'src': 'components',
75	        # ant-design commits no lockfile and sets package-lock=false, so there is nothing to freeze against.
76	        'manager': 'npm',
77	    },
78	    {
79	        'name': 'spectrum',
80	        'repo': 'adobe/react-spectrum',
81	        'commit': '797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70',
82	        'clone': 'react-spectrum',
83	        'src': 'packages',
84	        'manager': 'yarn',
85	    },
86	]
87	
88	REGRESSION_LIMIT = 1.1
89	# Rates may wobble by a prop or two when a corpus' component set shifts; anything larger is a regression.
90	RATE_TOLERANCE = 0.0005
91	COREPACK_VERSION = '0.34.0'
92	PRUNED_DIRS = {
93	    '__tests__', '__snapshots__', 'test', 'tests', 'stories', '__stories__', 'demo', '__demo__', 'docs', 'e2e',
94	    'dist', 'build', '.storybook', 'examples',
95	}
96	PRUNED_FILE = re.compile(r'\.(test|spec|stories|story)\.|\.d\.ts$')
97	
98	
99	# ─── Setup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
100	
101	
102	def package_manager_env(base):
103	    caches = os.path.join(base, 'caches')
104	    # The package managers corepack downloads (yarn 4's `yarn.js`) are CommonJS bundles. The corepack home lives under
105	    # this repository, whose root package.json says `"type": "module"`, so Node would load them as ES modules, where
106	    # `require` does not exist: `Dynamic require of "util" is not supported`. A package.json of their own wins.
107	    corepack_home = os.path.join(caches, 'corepack')
108	    os.makedirs(corepack_home, exist_ok=True)
109	    with open(os.path.join(corepack_home, 'package.json'), 'w') as manifest:
110	        manifest.write('{"type": "commonjs"}\n')
111	    env = dict(os.environ)
112	    env.update({
113	        'COREPACK_HOME': corepack_home,
114	        'COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT': '0',
115	        'COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN': '0',
116	        'YARN_CACHE_FOLDER': os.path.join(caches, 'yarn'),
117	        'YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER': os.path.join(caches, 'yarn-global'),
118	        'YARN_ENABLE_GLOBAL_CACHE': '0',
119	        'YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS': '0',
120	        'YARN_NODE_LINKER': 'node-modules',
121	        'YARN_ENABLE_TELEMETRY': '0',
122	        'npm_config_cache': os.path.join(caches, 'npm'),
123	        'PATH': os.path.join(base, 'tools', 'bin') + os.pathsep + os.environ.get('PATH', ''),
124	    })
125	    return env
126	
127	
128	def ensure_package_managers(base, env, log):
129	    """pnpm and yarn shims from corepack, at the versions each repo's `packageManager` pins."""
130	    bin_dir = os.path.join(base, 'tools', 'bin')
131	    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(bin_dir, 'pnpm')):
132	        return
133	    os.makedirs(bin_dir, exist_ok=True)
134	    corepack = shutil.which('corepack')
135	    if corepack is None:
136	        # Node 25 and later no longer bundle corepack.
137	        tools = os.path.join(base, 'tools')
138	        subprocess.run(['npm', 'install', '--prefix', tools, '--no-audit', '--no-fund', f'corepack@{COREPACK_VERSION}'],
139	                       env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log, check=True)
140	        corepack = os.path.join(tools, 'node_modules', '.bin', 'corepack')
141	    subprocess.run([corepack, 'enable', '--install-directory', bin_dir, 'pnpm', 'yarn'], env=env, check=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Caliper against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) on five public repos with their dependencies installed.

`setup` fetches each repo at its pinned commit, installs its dependencies with its own package manager and lockfile
(lifecycle scripts off, caches under the corpora directory), and prunes tests, stories and demos from the source
directory. `run` dumps RDT once per corpus (scripts/parity-rdt.mjs, cached by commit), runs Caliper in RDT's format
with and without --load-dependencies, and reports per corpus:

  - components RDT reports (with props) that Caliper also reports, by file and name;
  - RDT props not declared by @types/react that Caliper reports;
  - shared props whose type text is identical, identical after cosmetic normalization, or gives the same Storybook
    control;
  - shared props per loss pattern: Caliper's type carrying less than RDT's (a member read left as `X["k"]`, a lost
    rest parameter, ...), and two patterns where RDT carries less;
  - best-of-N wall time and peak RSS of `extract --json`, without and with --load-dependencies, next to RDT's.

--check against --baseline fails when coverage, agreement or same-control rates drop, a loss pattern grows, or BIN is
more than 1.1x slower than --base-bin (timed interleaved on the same machine).

`oracle` compares Caliper's canonical prop types with TypeScript 7.1's checker on the same corpora and the repo's
fixtures (apps/validate/src/oracle.ts), one verdict per shared prop: identical, spelled differently, less precise,
wrong, or no checker type. Its --check fails when agreement falls or wrong verdicts rise. It is test-only.

docs/parity.md explains the measures.

Usage: scripts/parity.py setup [--corpora DIR] [--corpus NAME]... [--install-node-dir DIR]
       scripts/parity.py run --bin BIN [--base-bin BIN] [--corpora DIR] [--rdt-dir DIR] [--corpus NAME]...
                             [--runs N] [--no-timing] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--baseline FILE] [--check]
       scripts/parity.py oracle --bin BIN [--corpora DIR] [--corpus NAME | fixtures]... [--work DIR] [--out FILE]
                                [--markdown FILE] [--baseline FILE] [--check]
"""
import argparse
import functools
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

CORPORA = [
    {
        'name': 'mantine',
        'repo': 'mantinedev/mantine',
        'commit': 'e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d',
        'clone': 'mantine',
        'src': 'packages/@mantine/core/src',
        'manager': 'yarn',
    },
    {
        'name': 'chakra',
        'repo': 'chakra-ui/chakra-ui',
        'commit': 'fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9',
        'clone': 'chakra-ui',
        'src': 'packages/react/src',
        'manager': 'pnpm',
    },
    {
        'name': 'shadcn',
        'repo': 'shadcn-ui/ui',
        'commit': 'ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b',
        'clone': 'shadcn-ui',
        'src': 'apps/v4',
        'manager': 'pnpm',
    },
    {
        'name': 'antd',
        'repo': 'ant-design/ant-design',
        'commit': 'ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538',
        'clone': 'ant-design',
        'src': 'components',
        # ant-design commits no lockfile and sets package-lock=false, so there is nothing to freeze against.
        'manager': 'npm',
    },
    {
        'name': 'spectrum',
        'repo': 'adobe/react-spectrum',
        'commit': '797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70',
        'clone': 'react-spectrum',
        'src': 'packages',
        'manager': 'yarn',
    },
]

REGRESSION_LIMIT = 1.1
# Rates may wobble by a prop or two when a corpus' component set shifts; anything larger is a regression.
RATE_TOLERANCE = 0.0005
COREPACK_VERSION = '0.34.0'
PRUNED_DIRS = {
    '__tests__', '__snapshots__', 'test', 'tests', 'stories', '__stories__', 'demo', '__demo__', 'docs', 'e2e',
    'dist', 'build', '.storybook', 'examples',
}
PRUNED_FILE = re.compile(r'\.(test|spec|stories|story)\.|\.d\.ts$')


# ─── Setup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def package_manager_env(base):
    caches = os.path.join(base, 'caches')
    # The package managers corepack downloads (yarn 4's `yarn.js`) are CommonJS bundles. The corepack home lives under
    # this repository, whose root package.json says `"type": "module"`, so Node would load them as ES modules, where
    # `require` does not exist: `Dynamic require of "util" is not supported`. A package.json of their own wins.
    corepack_home = os.path.join(caches, 'corepack')
    os.makedirs(corepack_home, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(corepack_home, 'package.json'), 'w') as manifest:
        manifest.write('{"type": "commonjs"}\n')
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update({
        'COREPACK_HOME': corepack_home,
        'COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT': '0',
        'COREPACK_ENABLE_AUTO_PIN': '0',
        'YARN_CACHE_FOLDER': os.path.join(caches, 'yarn'),
        'YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER': os.path.join(caches, 'yarn-global'),
        'YARN_ENABLE_GLOBAL_CACHE': '0',
        'YARN_ENABLE_SCRIPTS': '0',
        'YARN_NODE_LINKER': 'node-modules',
        'YARN_ENABLE_TELEMETRY': '0',
        'npm_config_cache': os.path.join(caches, 'npm'),
        'PATH': os.path.join(base, 'tools', 'bin') + os.pathsep + os.environ.get('PATH', ''),
    })
    return env


def ensure_package_managers(base, env, log):
    """pnpm and yarn shims from corepack, at the versions each repo's `packageManager` pins."""
    bin_dir = os.path.join(base, 'tools', 'bin')
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(bin_dir, 'pnpm')):
        return
    os.makedirs(bin_dir, exist_ok=True)
    corepack = shutil.which('corepack')
    if corepack is None:
        # Node 25 and later no longer bundle corepack.
        tools = os.path.join(base, 'tools')
        subprocess.run(['npm', 'install', '--prefix', tools, '--no-audit', '--no-fund', f'corepack@{COREPACK_VERSION}'],
                       env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log, check=True)
        corepack = os.path.join(tools, 'node_modules', '.bin', 'corepack')
    subprocess.run([corepack, 'enable', '--install-directory', bin_dir, 'pnpm', 'yarn'], env=env, check=True)


def git(*args, cwd):
    subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=cwd, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def fetch(corpus, checkout):
    shutil.rmtree(checkout, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(checkout)
    git('init', '-q', cwd=checkout)
    git('remote', 'add', 'origin', f"https://github.com/{corpus['repo']}.git", cwd=checkout)
    # Network steps retry: one dropped connection shouldn't fail a scheduled run.
    for attempt in range(3):
        try:
            git('fetch', '-q', '--depth', '1', 'origin', corpus['commit'], cwd=checkout)
            git('checkout', '-q', 'FETCH_HEAD', cwd=checkout)
            return
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            if attempt == 2:
                raise
            time.sleep(5)


def tail(path, lines=30):
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            return ''.join(f.readlines()[-lines:])
    except OSError:
        return ''


def install(corpus, checkout, base, env, log):
    caches = os.path.join(base, 'caches')
    pnpm = ['--store-dir', os.path.join(caches, 'pnpm-store'), f"--config.cache-dir={os.path.join(caches, 'pnpm-cache')}"]
    commands = {
        'pnpm': [['pnpm', 'install', '--frozen-lockfile', '--ignore-scripts', *pnpm],
                 ['pnpm', 'install', '--no-frozen-lockfile', '--ignore-scripts', *pnpm]],
        'yarn': [['yarn', 'install', '--immutable', '--mode=skip-build'],
                 ['yarn', 'install', '--no-immutable', '--mode=skip-build']],
        'npm': [['npm', 'install', '--ignore-scripts', '--no-audit', '--no-fund']],
    }[corpus['manager']]
    # The lockfile first; a lockfile the pinned package manager rejects falls back to resolving again.
    for command in commands:
        log.write(f"\n$ {' '.join(command)}  (node {subprocess.run(['node', '--version'], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()})\n")
        log.flush()
        if subprocess.run(command, cwd=checkout, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log, stderr=log).returncode == 0:
            return
    raise RuntimeError(f"{corpus['name']}: dependency install failed, see {log.name}")


def prune(src):
    """What neither tool should document, inside the source directory only. node_modules is never entered."""
    for current, dirs, files in os.walk(src, topdown=True):
        keep = []
        for d in dirs:
            if d == 'node_modules':
                continue
            if d in PRUNED_DIRS:
                shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(current, d))
            else:
                keep.append(d)
        dirs[:] = keep
        for f in files:
            if PRUNED_FILE.search(f):
                os.remove(os.path.join(current, f))


def setup(args):
    corpora_dir = os.path.abspath(args.corpora)
    base = os.path.dirname(corpora_dir)
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(base, 'logs'), exist_ok=True)
    env = package_manager_env(base)
    with open(os.path.join(base, 'logs', 'corepack.log'), 'w') as log:
        ensure_package_managers(base, env, log)
    # The corpora's own package managers can need an older Node than this repository's (Yarn 4.18, which Mantine and
    # React Spectrum pin, crashes under Node 26). Only their installs run under it.
    install_env = dict(env)
    if args.install_node_dir:
        install_env['PATH'] = os.path.abspath(args.install_node_dir) + os.pathsep + env['PATH']
    failed = []
    for corpus in selected(args.corpus):
        checkout = os.path.join(corpora_dir, corpus['clone'])
        marker = os.path.join(checkout, '.parity-complete')
        if os.path.exists(marker) and open(marker).read() == corpus['commit']:
            print(f"{corpus['name']}: ready at {corpus['commit'][:12]}")
            continue
        log_path = os.path.join(base, 'logs', f"install-{corpus['name']}.log")
        try:
            print(f"{corpus['name']}: fetching {corpus['commit'][:12]}", flush=True)
            fetch(corpus, checkout)
            print(f"{corpus['name']}: installing with {corpus['manager']}", flush=True)
            with open(log_path, 'w') as log:
                install(corpus, checkout, base, install_env, log)
            prune(os.path.join(checkout, corpus['src']))
            with open(marker, 'w') as f:
                f.write(corpus['commit'])
            print(f"{corpus['name']}: ready at {corpus['commit'][:12]}")
        except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, RuntimeError, OSError) as error:
            # One corpus failing must not hide the others: say which one and why, then carry on with the rest.
            failed.append(corpus['name'])
            reason = f"{corpus['name']}: setup FAILED ({error})"
            print(f"{reason}\n--- last lines of {log_path}\n{tail(log_path)}---", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            if os.environ.get('GITHUB_ACTIONS'):
                print(f"::error title=Parity corpus {corpus['name']} failed to set up::{error}", flush=True)
    if failed:
        summary = os.environ.get('GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY')
        if summary:
            with open(summary, 'a') as f:
                f.write(f"### Corpus setup failed\n\n{', '.join(failed)}: see the install logs in the parity artifact.\n")
        sys.exit(f"setup failed for: {', '.join(failed)}")


# ─── Measures ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def norm_name(name):
    """A component name as both tools may spell it: no `(file)` suffix, namespace or punctuation."""
    name = re.sub(r' \(.*\)$', '', name).split('/')[-1].split('.')[-1]
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]', '', name.lower())

380	def measure(rdt, mine, clone_root):
381	    """The coverage, agreement and loss-pattern counts of one Caliper run against RDT's dump."""
382	    by_file = {}
383	    for c in mine.values():
384	        rel = relative(c['filePath'], clone_root)
385	        by_file.setdefault(rel, []).append((norm_name(c['displayName']), c))
386	    counts = {
387	        'rdt_components': 0, 'components_matched': 0, 'rdt_props': 0, 'props_reported': 0,
388	        'shared': 0, 'same_text': 0, 'same_or_cosmetic': 0, 'same_control': 0,
389	    }
390	    loss = {label: 0 for label in LOSS_PATTERNS}
391	    rdt_loss = {label: 0 for label in RDT_LOSS_PATTERNS}
392	    for comp in rdt:
393	        if not comp['props']:
394	            continue
395	        counts['rdt_components'] += 1
396	        m = next((c for n, c in by_file.get(comp['file'], []) if n == norm_name(comp['name'])), None)
397	        if m is None:
398	            continue
399	        counts['components_matched'] += 1
400	        for prop, info in comp['props'].items():
401	            theirs = info['type'] if isinstance(info['type'], str) else json.dumps(info['type'])
402	            react = 'node_modules/@types/react/' in (info.get('parent') or '')
403	            if not react:
404	                counts['rdt_props'] += 1
405	            if prop not in m['props']:
406	                continue
407	            ours = m['props'][prop]['type']['name']
408	            if not react:
409	                counts['props_reported'] += 1
410	                counts['shared'] += 1
411	                same = base_text(ours) == base_text(theirs)
412	                counts['same_text'] += same
413	                counts['same_or_cosmetic'] += same or cosmetic(ours) == cosmetic(theirs)
414	                counts['same_control'] += control(ours) == control(theirs)
415	            o, r = ours.replace('React.', ''), theirs.replace('React.', '')
416	            for label, test in LOSS_PATTERNS.items():
417	                loss[label] += bool(test(o, r))
418	            for label, test in RDT_LOSS_PATTERNS.items():
419	                rdt_loss[label] += bool(test(o, r))
420	    return {**counts, 'loss': loss, 'rdt_loss': rdt_loss}

423	def run_once(args):
424	    """Wall seconds and peak RSS in MiB of one process."""
425	    start = time.time()
426	    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
427	    _, status, usage = os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)
428	    elapsed = time.time() - start
429	    proc.returncode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
430	    if proc.returncode != 0:
431	        raise RuntimeError(f'{args} exited with {proc.returncode}')
432	    # ru_maxrss is bytes on macOS and kilobytes on Linux.
433	    rss = usage.ru_maxrss / 2**20 if sys.platform == 'darwin' else usage.ru_maxrss / 1024
434	    return elapsed, rss

437	def timings(binaries, src, runs):
438	    """Best-of-N wall ms and peak RSS for each binary, with and without --load-dependencies, runs interleaved."""
439	    result = {}
440	    for deps in (False, True):
441	        mode = 'on' if deps else 'off'
442	        best = {label: (float('inf'), 0.0) for label in binaries}
443	        for label, binary in binaries.items():
444	            subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json'] + deps_flags(binary, deps),
445	                           capture_output=True, check=True)
446	        for _ in range(runs):
447	            for label, binary in binaries.items():
448	                args = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json'] + deps_flags(binary, deps)
449	                elapsed, rss = run_once(args)
450	                ms, peak = best[label]
451	                best[label] = (min(ms, elapsed * 1000), max(peak, rss))
452	        for label, (ms, rss) in best.items():
453	            result.setdefault(label, {})[mode] = {'ms': round(ms, 1), 'rss_mib': round(rss, 1)}
454	    return result

567	def oracle_check(report, baseline):
568	    """Each oracle gate that fails: fewer props agreeing with the checker, or more that it contradicts."""
569	    failures = []
570	    for name, e in report['corpora'].items():

575	        wrong = lambda x: rate(x['verdicts']['wrong'], x['props_shared'])

584	            failures.append(f'{name}: components matched fell from {100 * matched(old):.2f}% to '

675	def check(report, baseline):
676	    """Each gate that fails, as a message."""
677	    failures = []
678	    for name, entry in report['corpora'].items():
679	        old = baseline.get('corpora', {}).get(name)
680	        for mode, m in entry['modes'].items():
681	            if old is None or mode not in old['modes']:
682	                continue
683	            o = old['modes'][mode]
684	            for label, (num, den) in {
685	                'components matched': ('components_matched', 'rdt_components'),
686	                'props reported': ('props_reported', 'rdt_props'),
687	                'same text': ('same_text', 'shared'),
688	                'same or cosmetic': ('same_or_cosmetic', 'shared'),
689	                'same control': ('same_control', 'shared'),
690	            }.items():
691	                now, before = rate(m[num], m[den]), rate(o[num], o[den])
692	                if now < before - RATE_TOLERANCE:
693	                    failures.append(f'{name} ({mode}): {label} fell from {100 * before:.2f}% to {100 * now:.2f}%')
694	            for label, count in m['loss'].items():
695	                before = o['loss'].get(label)
696	                if before is not None and count > before:
697	                    failures.append(f'{name} ({mode}): "{label}" grew from {before:,} to {count:,} props')
698	        timing = entry.get('timing', {})
699	        if 'base' in timing:
700	            for mode in ('off', 'on'):
701	                head, base = timing['head'][mode]['ms'], timing['base'][mode]['ms']
702	                if head > REGRESSION_LIMIT * base:
703	                    failures.append(f'{name} ({mode}): {head:.0f} ms is more than {REGRESSION_LIMIT}x the base '
704	                                    f'build ({base:.0f} ms)')
705	    return failures

        if old is None:
            continue
        agree = lambda x: rate(x['verdicts']['identical'] + x['verdicts']['spelled'], x['props_shared'])
        wrong = lambda x: rate(x['verdicts']['wrong'], x['props_shared'])
        matched = lambda x: rate(x['components_matched'], x['components_checker'])
        if agree(e) < agree(old) - RATE_TOLERANCE:
            failures.append(f'{name}: props agreeing with the checker fell from {100 * agree(old):.2f}% to '
                            f'{100 * agree(e):.2f}%')
        if wrong(e) > wrong(old) + RATE_TOLERANCE:
            failures.append(f'{name}: props the checker contradicts rose from {100 * wrong(old):.2f}% to '
                            f'{100 * wrong(e):.2f}%')
        if matched(e) < matched(old) - RATE_TOLERANCE:
            failures.append(f'{name}: components matched fell from {100 * matched(old):.2f}% to '
                            f'{100 * matched(e):.2f}%')
    return failures


def selected(names):
    if not names:
        return CORPORA
    unknown = set(names) - {c['name'] for c in CORPORA}
    if unknown:
        sys.exit(f"unknown corpus: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    return [c for c in CORPORA if c['name'] in names]


def run(args):
    corpora_dir = os.path.abspath(args.corpora)
    version = subprocess.run([args.bin, '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    report = {'caliper': version, 'runs': args.runs, 'corpora': {}}
    for corpus in selected(args.corpus):
        clone_root = os.path.join(corpora_dir, corpus['clone'])
        src = os.path.join(clone_root, corpus['src'])
        if not os.path.isdir(src):
            sys.exit(f"{corpus['name']}: {src} is missing; run `scripts/parity.py setup` first")
        dump = rdt_dump(corpus, src, clone_root, os.path.abspath(args.rdt_dir))
        entry = {
            'commit': corpus['commit'],
            'rdt': {'ms': round(dump['wallMs'], 1), 'rss_mib': round(dump['peakRssMiB'], 1)},
            'modes': {},
        }
        for deps in (False, True):
            print(f"{corpus['name']}: measuring, dependencies {'on' if deps else 'off'}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            entry['modes']['on' if deps else 'off'] = measure(dump['components'], caliper_rdt(args.bin, src, deps),
                                                              clone_root)
        if not args.no_timing:
            binaries = {'head': args.bin, **({'base': args.base_bin} if args.base_bin else {})}
            print(f"{corpus['name']}: timing", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            entry['timing'] = timings(binaries, src, args.runs)
        report['corpora'][corpus['name']] = entry
    return report


# ─── Report and gates ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def rate(a, b):
    return a / b if b else 0.0


def pct(a, b):
    return f'{100 * rate(a, b):.1f}%'


def markdown(report):
    lines = [f"Caliper {report['caliper']}, best of {report['runs']} runs.", '']
    for mode, title in (('on', 'with --load-dependencies'), ('off', 'without dependencies')):
        lines += [f'### Against RDT, {title}', '',
                  '| Corpus | Components matched | Non-React props reported | Same text | Same or cosmetic | '
                  'Same control |', '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
        for name, entry in report['corpora'].items():
            m = entry['modes'][mode]
            lines.append(
                f"| {name} | {m['components_matched']}/{m['rdt_components']} | "
                f"{m['props_reported']:,}/{m['rdt_props']:,} ({pct(m['props_reported'], m['rdt_props'])}) | "
                f"{pct(m['same_text'], m['shared'])} | {pct(m['same_or_cosmetic'], m['shared'])} | "
                f"{pct(m['same_control'], m['shared'])} |")
        lines.append('')
    names = list(report['corpora'])
    lines += ['### Loss patterns, with --load-dependencies (shared props)', '',
              '| Pattern | ' + ' | '.join(names) + ' |', '| --- |' + ' --: |' * len(names)]
    first = report['corpora'][names[0]]['modes']['on']
    for group in ('loss', 'rdt_loss'):
        for label in first[group]:
            suffix = ' (RDT carries less)' if group == 'rdt_loss' else ''
            cells = [f"{report['corpora'][n]['modes']['on'][group][label]:,}" for n in names]
            lines.append(f'| {label}{suffix} | ' + ' | '.join(cells) + ' |')
    lines.append('')
    if all('timing' in e for e in report['corpora'].values()):
        lines += ['### Time and memory', '',
                  '| Corpus | Caliper default | Caliper --load-dependencies | Base default | Base --load-dependencies | '
                  'RDT (dependencies resolvable) |', '| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |']
        for name, entry in report['corpora'].items():
            t = entry['timing']
            cell = lambda r: f"{r['ms']:.0f} ms, {r['rss_mib']:.0f} MiB"
            base = t.get('base')
            lines.append(f"| {name} | {cell(t['head']['off'])} | {cell(t['head']['on'])} | "
                         f"{cell(base['off']) if base else '-'} | {cell(base['on']) if base else '-'} | "
                         f"{entry['rdt']['ms'] / 1000:.1f} s, {entry['rdt']['rss_mib']:,.0f} MiB |")
        lines.append('')
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def check(report, baseline):
    """Each gate that fails, as a message."""
    failures = []
    for name, entry in report['corpora'].items():
        old = baseline.get('corpora', {}).get(name)
        for mode, m in entry['modes'].items():
            if old is None or mode not in old['modes']:
                continue
            o = old['modes'][mode]
            for label, (num, den) in {
                'components matched': ('components_matched', 'rdt_components'),
                'props reported': ('props_reported', 'rdt_props'),
                'same text': ('same_text', 'shared'),
                'same or cosmetic': ('same_or_cosmetic', 'shared'),
                'same control': ('same_control', 'shared'),
            }.items():
                now, before = rate(m[num], m[den]), rate(o[num], o[den])
                if now < before - RATE_TOLERANCE:
                    failures.append(f'{name} ({mode}): {label} fell from {100 * before:.2f}% to {100 * now:.2f}%')
            for label, count in m['loss'].items():
                before = o['loss'].get(label)
                if before is not None and count > before:
                    failures.append(f'{name} ({mode}): "{label}" grew from {before:,} to {count:,} props')
        timing = entry.get('timing', {})
        if 'base' in timing:
            for mode in ('off', 'on'):
                head, base = timing['head'][mode]['ms'], timing['base'][mode]['ms']
                if head > REGRESSION_LIMIT * base:
                    failures.append(f'{name} ({mode}): {head:.0f} ms is more than {REGRESSION_LIMIT}x the base '
                                    f'build ({base:.0f} ms)')
    return failures


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', required=True)
    default_corpora = os.path.join(ROOT, '.parity', 'corpora')
    p_setup = sub.add_parser('setup', help='fetch, install and prune the corpora')
    p_setup.add_argument('--corpora', default=default_corpora)
    p_setup.add_argument('--corpus', action='append', default=[])
    p_setup.add_argument('--install-node-dir', help="a directory with the `node` the corpora's installs should use")
    p_run = sub.add_parser('run', help='measure a build against RDT')
    p_run.add_argument('--bin', required=True)
    p_run.add_argument('--base-bin')
    p_run.add_argument('--corpora', default=default_corpora)
    p_run.add_argument('--rdt-dir', default=os.path.join(ROOT, '.parity', 'rdt'))
    p_run.add_argument('--corpus', action='append', default=[])
    p_run.add_argument('--runs', type=int, default=7)
    p_run.add_argument('--no-timing', action='store_true')
    p_run.add_argument('--out')
    p_run.add_argument('--markdown')
    p_run.add_argument('--baseline')
    p_run.add_argument('--check', action='store_true')
    p_oracle = sub.add_parser('oracle', help="compare a build's prop types with TypeScript 7.1's checker")
    p_oracle.add_argument('--bin', required=True)
    p_oracle.add_argument('--corpora', default=default_corpora)
    p_oracle.add_argument('--corpus', action='append', default=[], help='a corpus name, or fixtures')
    p_oracle.add_argument('--work', default=os.path.join(ROOT, '.parity', 'oracle'))
    p_oracle.add_argument('--out')
    p_oracle.add_argument('--markdown')
    p_oracle.add_argument('--baseline')
    p_oracle.add_argument('--check', action='store_true')
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.command == 'setup':
        setup(args)
        return
    if args.command == 'oracle':
        report = oracle(args)
        table, gates = oracle_markdown(report), oracle_check
    else:
        report = run(args)
        table, gates = markdown(report), check
    print(table, flush=True)
    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
            f.write('\n')
    if args.markdown:
        with open(args.markdown, 'w') as f:
            f.write(table + '\n')
    if args.check:
        if not args.baseline:
            sys.exit('--check needs --baseline')
        with open(args.baseline) as f:
            failures = gates(report, json.load(f))
        if failures:
            print('\nGates failed:\n' + '\n'.join(f'- {f}' for f in failures), file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
        print('\nAll gates passed.', file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

name: Parity

# Caliper against react-docgen-typescript on five public repos with their dependencies installed (docs/parity.md).
# The installs are heavy, so this runs weekly and by hand rather than on every pull request. It compares this commit's
# build with main's, timed interleaved in one job, and gates on scripts/parity-baseline.json.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      base:
        description: Ref to compare against (default main)
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"

jobs:
  parity:
    name: Parity
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      # main's list must be empty. A run dispatched on a branch carries that branch's own entries on purpose, so there
      # the step only reports: failing it would skip the install, the build and every measurement after it.
      - name: Allow-list is empty
        continue-on-error: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
        run: python3 scripts/equivalence.py --require-empty-allow
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      # The corpora's own package managers run under Node 24: Yarn 4.18, which Mantine and React Spectrum pin, crashes
      # under the repository's Node 26 ("Dynamic require of "util" is not supported"). This step comes before the
      # toolchain's so that the toolchain's Node stays first on PATH for everything else; only the installs use this one.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          package-manager-cache: false
      - id: corpus-node
        run: echo "dir=$(dirname "$(command -v node)")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # RDT runs from apps/validate's react-docgen-typescript.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - id: base
        env:
          BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
        run: |
          ref="origin/${BASE:-main}"
          git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$ref^{commit}" >/dev/null || ref="$BASE"
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse --verify "$ref^{commit}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Build this commit and the base
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.base.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
          cp target/release/caliper-docgen "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head"
          git worktree add --detach "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" "$BASE_SHA"
          cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen --manifest-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/Cargo.toml" --target-dir target
          cp target/release/caliper-docgen "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-base"
      # About 10 GB of installed node_modules is too large to cache; the package managers' stores and RDT's dumps,
      # which are keyed by commit, are not.
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            .parity/caches
            .parity/rdt
          key: parity-${{ hashFiles('scripts/parity.py', 'scripts/parity-rdt.mjs', 'pnpm-lock.yaml') }}
      # A corpus that fails to install is named in the log, an annotation and the job summary with the tail of its install
      # log; the others still install. The install logs are in the parity artifact.
      - name: Fetch and install the corpora
        env:
          INSTALL_NODE_DIR: ${{ steps.corpus-node.outputs.dir }}
        run: python3 scripts/parity.py setup --install-node-dir "$INSTALL_NODE_DIR"
      - name: Measure and gate
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/parity.py run --bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head" --base-bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-base"
          --baseline scripts/parity-baseline.json --out parity.json --markdown parity.md --check
      # TypeScript 7.1's checker as the oracle for prop types (test-only; apps/validate/src/oracle.ts).
      - name: Compare prop types with TypeScript's checker
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/parity.py oracle --bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head" --baseline scripts/oracle-baseline.json
          --out oracle.json --markdown oracle.md --check
      # Does this commit publish what the base does? All five corpora, four configurations, and the lazy session
      # against batch extraction (scripts/equivalence.py).
      - name: Compare output with the base
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/equivalence.py "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-base" --bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head"
          --markdown equivalence.md
      - if: always()
        run: cat parity.md oracle.md equivalence.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: parity
          path: |
            parity.json
            parity.md
            oracle.json
            oracle.md
            equivalence.md
            .parity/logs

1	// react-docgen-typescript on one parity corpus (scripts/parity.py): every component's props with their declaring file,
2	// plus RDT's own wall time and peak RSS. RDT comes from apps/validate, with the options its harness uses.
3	//
4	// Usage: node scripts/parity-rdt.mjs <file-list> <tsconfig> <out.json>
5	import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
6	import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
7	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
8	
9	const require = createRequire(fileURLToPath(new URL('../apps/validate/package.json', import.meta.url)))
10	const { withCustomConfig } = require('react-docgen-typescript')
11	
12	const [listFile, tsconfig, out] = process.argv.slice(2)
13	if (!out) {
14	  console.error('usage: node scripts/parity-rdt.mjs <file-list> <tsconfig> <out.json>')
15	  process.exit(2)
16	}
17	const files = readFileSync(listFile, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean)
18	const start = performance.now()
19	const parser = withCustomConfig(tsconfig, {
20	  shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum: true,
21	  shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional: true,
22	  propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false },
23	})
24	const docs = parser.parse(files)
25	const wallMs = performance.now() - start
26	const components = docs.map((d) => ({
27	  file: d.filePath,
28	  name: d.displayName,
29	  props: Object.fromEntries(
30	    Object.entries(d.props ?? {}).map(([k, p]) => [
31	      k,
32	      {
33	        required: Boolean(p.required),
34	        type: p.type?.name ?? '',
35	        parent: p.parent?.fileName ?? p.declarations?.[0]?.fileName ?? '',
36	      },
37	    ]),
38	  ),
39	}))
40	// `maxRSS` is in kilobytes on every platform Node supports.
41	const peakRssMiB = process.resourceUsage().maxRSS / 1024
42	writeFileSync(out, JSON.stringify({ wallMs, peakRssMiB, components }))
43	console.error(`dumped ${components.length} components in ${(wallMs / 1000).toFixed(1)} s, ${peakRssMiB.toFixed(0)} MiB`)
44

1	import { parse } from 'react-docgen'
2	import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
3	import { discoverFixtures } from './fixtures.ts'
4	import type { ToolResult, NormalizedOutput } from './types.ts'
5	
6	// react-docgen puts real TypeScript type info under `tsType`, not `type` —
7	// `type` is the legacy PropTypes-oriented field (`PropTypes.string` etc.) and
8	// is simply absent for interface/type-annotated TS props, so reading it alone
9	// silently produced "unknown" for every TS-typed prop. `tsType.raw` carries
10	// the exact original source text (`'primary' | 'secondary'`, `string[]`,
11	// `(id: string) => void`) when TS can print it, which is the fairest
12	// comparison against our own type-to-string rendering — falls back to
13	// `tsType.name` for the cases where `raw` isn't present (plain primitives).
14	function rdgTypeToString(prop: any): string {
15	  const t = prop.tsType ?? prop.type
16	  if (!t) return 'unknown'
17	  return t.raw ?? t.name ?? 'unknown'
18	}
19	
20	function normalize(rdgOutput: any[]): NormalizedOutput {
21	  const result: NormalizedOutput = {}
22	  for (const comp of rdgOutput) {
23	    const name = comp.displayName ?? 'Unknown'
24	    result[name] = {
25	      displayName: name,
26	      description: comp.description ?? '',
27	      props: Object.fromEntries(
28	        Object.entries(comp.props ?? {}).map(([propName, prop]: [string, any]) => [
29	          propName,
30	          {
31	            name: propName,
32	            required: prop.required ?? false,
33	            type: rdgTypeToString(prop),
34	            description: prop.description ?? '',
35	            defaultValue: prop.defaultValue?.value,
36	          },
37	        ]),
38	      ),
39	    }
40	  }
41	  return result
42	}
43	
44	const fixtures = discoverFixtures().filter((f) => f.isTsx)
45	const results: ToolResult[] = []
46	
47	for (const fixture of fixtures) {
48	  const source = readFileSync(fixture.path, 'utf8')
49	  const start = performance.now()
50	  try {
51	    const raw = parse(source, { filename: fixture.path })
52	    const durationMs = performance.now() - start
53	    const comps = Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : [raw]
54	    // One entry per component, keyed `${fixture.name}/${displayName}` — matches
55	    // rdt's and ours' keying. Previously this pushed one ToolResult per FILE
56	    // (keyed by fixture.name alone, with every component packed into its
57	    // `output`), which never joined against rdt/ours' per-component keys in
58	    // compare.ts — a multi-component file silently broke the join for every
59	    // component in it, and even single-component files only "matched" by
60	    // accident of an exact string comparison that never actually held.
61	    for (const comp of comps) {
62	      const name = comp.displayName ?? 'Unknown'
63	      results.push({
64	        tool: 'react-docgen',
65	        fixture: `${fixture.name}/${name}`,
66	        durationMs,
67	        output: normalize([comp]),
68	      })
69	    }
70	    if (comps.length === 0) {
71	      results.push({ tool: 'react-docgen', fixture: fixture.name, durationMs, output: {} })
72	    }
73	  } catch (error: any) {
74	    results.push({
75	      tool: 'react-docgen',
76	      fixture: fixture.name,
77	      durationMs: performance.now() - start,
78	      output: {},
79	      error: error.message,
80	    })
81	  }
82	}
83	
84	console.log(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproducible performance scorecard on five public corpora, with the gates docs/performance.md describes.

Fetches each corpus at its pinned commit (shallow, sparse: the source directory plus the files above it, no
dependencies installed), then for each one records lines of code, components, props, unresolved-type diagnostics, and
the median wall time and peak RSS of `caliper-docgen extract --json` with a warm parse cache. Every figure is with
dependency loading off (`--no-load-dependencies`, whatever the build's default), since nothing is installed; a build
that has the flag is also timed in its default mode, as the "With dependencies loading" column.

Optional comparisons:
  --base-bin BIN    a second build (main) timed interleaved with BIN on the same machine
  --rdt             time react-docgen-typescript on the same files (scripts/scorecard-rdt.mjs)
  --rdt-baseline F  read RDT times from a committed scorecard JSON instead

--check exits 1 when a gate fails: BIN slower than 1.1x BASE on any corpus, BIN less than 10x faster than RDT on any
corpus, BIN with dependency loading more than 1.7x its time without it, or two copies of Mantine taking more than 2.2x
as long as one (the scaling test).

Usage: scripts/scorecard.py --bin BIN [--base-bin BIN] [--rdt | --rdt-baseline FILE] [--runs N] [--corpora DIR]
                            [--out FILE] [--check]
"""
import argparse
import functools
import json
import os
import shutil
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

CORPORA = [
    {
        'name': 'mantine',
        'repo': 'mantinedev/mantine',
        'commit': '194d652452ee060aad3796c121f9b6a9f74cb453',
        'src': 'packages/@mantine/core/src',
    },
    {
        'name': 'chakra',
        'repo': 'chakra-ui/chakra-ui',
        'commit': '960ae222ace1df8de835dc3c62d698f1b58b6786',
        'src': 'packages/react/src',
    },
    {
        'name': 'shadcn',
        'repo': 'shadcn-ui/ui',
        'commit': '3d98900e9b73c45f035f8109e9d41ba6a51685e7',
        'src': 'apps/v4',
    },
    {
        'name': 'antd',
        'repo': 'ant-design/ant-design',
        'commit': 'f8f5595ab5e891fff6a2a06c5b3b98af643d008e',
        'src': 'components',
    },
    {
        'name': 'spectrum',
        'repo': 'adobe/react-spectrum',
        'commit': 'd5fb723a1c192e3a1a25c8cfdd4e26b900995307',
        'src': 'packages',
    },
]

# Diagnostics that mean a type was left unresolved, counted when they are warnings or errors.
UNRESOLVED_CODES = {
    'UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT',
    'OPAQUE_TYPE',
    'INDEXED_ACCESS_OPAQUE',
    'TEMPLATE_LITERAL_OPAQUE',
    'GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH',
    'UNKNOWN',
}

# Extraction ms = FIXED_MS + PER_KLOC_MS * kLOC + PER_KPROP_MS * kprops: a sizing guide, reported, not a gate
# (docs/performance.md).
FIXED_MS, PER_KLOC_MS, PER_KPROP_MS = 6.4, 0.13, 3.8
REGRESSION_LIMIT = 1.1
# Dependency loading with nothing installed: every import fails after a directory walk and the index keeps only answers
# found inside a package, so each run repeats them. Measured 1.15x to 1.2x on a laptop and up to about 1.5x on a CI
# runner; the limit catches a real jump, not that cost.
DEPS_LIMIT = 1.7
RDT_MIN_SPEEDUP = 10.0
SCALING_CORPUS = 'mantine'
SCALING_LIMIT = 2.2

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def git(*args, cwd):
    subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=cwd, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def fetch(corpus, corpora_dir):
    """The corpus' source directory, fetched once per pinned commit and source directory."""
    checkout = os.path.join(corpora_dir, f"{corpus['name']}-{corpus['commit'][:12]}")
    src = os.path.join(checkout, corpus['src'])
    marker = os.path.join(checkout, '.scorecard-complete')
    if os.path.exists(marker):
        with open(marker) as f:
            if f.read() == corpus['src']:
                return src
    shutil.rmtree(checkout, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(checkout)
    git('init', '-q', cwd=checkout)
    git('remote', 'add', 'origin', f"https://github.com/{corpus['repo']}.git", cwd=checkout)
    git('sparse-checkout', 'set', corpus['src'], cwd=checkout)
    # Network steps retry: one dropped connection shouldn't fail a scheduled run.
    for attempt in range(3):
        try:
            git('fetch', '-q', '--depth', '1', '--filter=blob:none', 'origin', corpus['commit'], cwd=checkout)
            git('checkout', '-q', 'FETCH_HEAD', cwd=checkout)
            break
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            if attempt == 2:
                raise
            time.sleep(5)
    with open(marker, 'w') as f:
        f.write(corpus['src'])
    return src


def excluded(relative):
    """The same exclusions as crates/core/src/pipeline/discover.rs."""
    name = os.path.basename(relative)
    parts = relative.split(os.sep)
    return (
        '.stories.' in name
        or '.test.' in name
        or '.spec.' in name
        or '__snapshots__' in parts
        or 'node_modules' in parts
    )


def lines_of_code(src):
    total = 0
    for dirpath, _, names in os.walk(src):
        for name in names:
            path = os.path.join(dirpath, name)
            if name.endswith(('.ts', '.tsx')) and not excluded(os.path.relpath(path, src)):
                with open(path, 'rb') as f:
                    total += f.read().count(b'\n')
    return total


def measure(cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL):
    """Wall time in ms and peak RSS in MB of one run of `cmd`."""
    start = time.perf_counter()
    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=stdout, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    _, status, usage = os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)
    elapsed = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    proc.returncode = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
    if proc.returncode not in (0, 1):
        sys.exit(f'{" ".join(cmd)} exited {proc.returncode}')
    # ru_maxrss is bytes on macOS, kilobytes on Linux.
    rss = usage.ru_maxrss / (1024 * 1024 if sys.platform == 'darwin' else 1024)
    return elapsed, rss


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def has_deps_flag(binary):
    """Whether `binary` knows `--no-load-dependencies` (builds from before dependency loading became the default don't)."""
    help_text = subprocess.run([binary, 'extract', '--help'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return '--no-load-dependencies' in help_text


def extract_command(binary, src, cache, deps=False):
    """`extract --json` over `src`. The corpora are fetched without their dependencies, so the scorecard measures with
    dependency loading off, whatever the binary's default; a build from before the flag existed is already off. The HTML
    attributes are `none`, so the gate times the resolver on the work main did; the cost of listing them is in ADR 0024."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--json', '-s', src, '--cache-dir', cache, '--html-attributes', 'none']
    if not deps and has_deps_flag(binary):
        command.append('--no-load-dependencies')
    return command


def counts(binary, src, cache):
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        measure(extract_command(binary, src, cache), stdout=out)
        out.seek(0)
        output = json.load(out)
    components = output['components'].values()
    return {
        'components': len(components),
        'props': sum(len(component['props']) for component in components),
        'unresolved': sum(
            1
            for d in output['diagnostics']
            if d['code'] in UNRESOLVED_CODES and d['severity'] != 'info'
        ),
    }


def timed_run(binary, src, cache, deps=False):
    """Wall ms, peak RSS MB, and the extraction's own `durationMs` of one run."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as out:
        wall, rss = measure(extract_command(binary, src, cache, deps), stdout=out)
        out.seek(0)

2	
3	# The performance gates in docs/performance.md, on five pinned public corpora. Weekly, the week's main is compared
4	# with main as of a week before; run it by hand on a branch to compare it with main. A pull request that touches the
5	# resolver, extractor, types or pipeline is compared with its own base on Mantine and Chakra, non-blocking until it has
6	# run green on ten pull requests (docs/performance.md): a speed regression of 38% and 47% on those two merged unseen.
7	on:
8	  schedule:
9	    - cron: "0 5 * * 1"
10	  pull_request:
11	    paths:
12	      - "crates/core/src/resolver/**"
13	      - "crates/core/src/extractor/**"
14	      - "crates/core/src/types/**"
15	      - "crates/core/src/pipeline/**"
16	      - "crates/core/src/dependency_types/**"
17	      - "scripts/scorecard*"
18	      - ".github/workflows/scorecard.yml"
19	  workflow_dispatch:
20	    inputs:
21	      base:
22	        description: Ref to compare against (default main; a scheduled run uses main as of 7 days ago)
23	        required: false
24	
25	permissions:
26	  contents: read
27	
28	concurrency:
29	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
30	  cancel-in-progress: true
31	
32	env:
33	  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
34	  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
35	
36	jobs:
37	  scorecard:
38	    name: Scorecard
39	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
40	    timeout-minutes: 60
41	    # A pull request's result is in the job summary; it does not fail the pull request yet.
42	    continue-on-error: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
43	    steps:
44	      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
45	        with:
46	          fetch-depth: 0
47	          persist-credentials: false
48	      - id: rust
49	        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
50	      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
51	        with:
52	          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
53	      # RDT is timed from apps/validate's react-docgen-typescript.
54	      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
55	        with:
56	          auto-install: true
57	      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
58	      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
59	      - id: base
60	        env:
61	          BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
62	          PR_BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
63	        run: |
64	          if [ -n "$PR_BASE" ]; then
65	            ref="origin/$PR_BASE"
66	          elif [ -n "$BASE" ]; then
67	            ref="origin/$BASE"
68	            git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$ref^{commit}" >/dev/null || ref="$BASE"
69	          elif [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = schedule ]; then
70	            ref="$(git rev-list -1 --before='7 days ago' origin/main)"
71	          else
72	            ref=origin/main
73	          fi
74	          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse --verify "$ref^{commit}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
75	      - name: Build this commit and the base
76	        env:
77	          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.base.outputs.sha }}
78	        run: |
79	          cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
80	          cp target/release/caliper-docgen "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head"

name: Scorecard

# The performance gates in docs/performance.md, on five pinned public corpora. Weekly, the week's main is compared
# with main as of a week before; run it by hand on a branch to compare it with main. A pull request that touches the
# resolver, extractor, types or pipeline is compared with its own base on Mantine and Chakra, non-blocking until it has
# run green on ten pull requests (docs/performance.md): a speed regression of 38% and 47% on those two merged unseen.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 5 * * 1"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "crates/core/src/resolver/**"
      - "crates/core/src/extractor/**"
      - "crates/core/src/types/**"
      - "crates/core/src/pipeline/**"
      - "crates/core/src/dependency_types/**"
      - "scripts/scorecard*"
      - ".github/workflows/scorecard.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      base:
        description: Ref to compare against (default main; a scheduled run uses main as of 7 days ago)
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"

jobs:
  scorecard:
    name: Scorecard
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    # A pull request's result is in the job summary; it does not fail the pull request yet.
    continue-on-error: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      # RDT is timed from apps/validate's react-docgen-typescript.
      - uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095 # v0.6.4
        with:
          auto-install: true
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-pnpm-cache@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - id: base
        env:
          BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
          PR_BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$PR_BASE" ]; then
            ref="origin/$PR_BASE"
          elif [ -n "$BASE" ]; then
            ref="origin/$BASE"
            git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$ref^{commit}" >/dev/null || ref="$BASE"
          elif [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = schedule ]; then
            ref="$(git rev-list -1 --before='7 days ago' origin/main)"
          else
            ref=origin/main
          fi
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse --verify "$ref^{commit}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Build this commit and the base
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.base.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
          cp target/release/caliper-docgen "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head"
          git worktree add --detach "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" "$BASE_SHA"
          cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen --manifest-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/Cargo.toml" --target-dir target
          cp target/release/caliper-docgen "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-base"
      - uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .scorecard/corpora
          key: scorecard-corpora-${{ hashFiles('scripts/scorecard.py') }}
      - name: Score and gate
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          # A pull request scores the two corpora where the last regression showed; the scaling gate needs mantine.
          only=()
          if [ "$EVENT" = pull_request ]; then only=(--corpus mantine --corpus chakra); fi
          python3 scripts/scorecard.py --bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-head" --base-bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/caliper-base" --rdt \
            "${only[@]}" --out scorecard.json --check
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: scorecard
          path: scorecard.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore

"""Tests for the loss patterns in scripts/parity.py. Run: python3 scripts/test_parity.py"""

import importlib.util
import os
import sys
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('parity', os.path.join(HERE, 'parity.py'))
parity = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules['parity'] = parity
spec.loader.exec_module(parity)


class UnboundTypeParameter(unittest.TestCase):
    pattern = staticmethod(parity.LOSS_PATTERNS['unbound type parameter'])

    def test_a_parameter_RDT_does_not_name_is_a_loss(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.pattern('T | string', 'string | NumberInputNumericType'))

    def test_single_capital_letters_inside_string_literals_are_not_parameters(self):
        self.assertEqual(parity.type_params('"S" | "M" | "L"'), set())
        self.assertFalse(self.pattern('"S" | "M" | "L"', 'string'))

    def test_a_parameter_beside_string_literals_is_still_found(self):
        self.assertEqual(parity.type_params('"a" | T'), {'T'})


class RestParameterLost(unittest.TestCase):
    pattern = staticmethod(parity.LOSS_PATTERNS['rest parameter lost'])

    def test_a_dropped_rest_parameter_is_a_loss(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.pattern('(args: any[]) => void', '(...args: any[]) => void'))

    def test_a_kept_rest_parameter_is_not(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.pattern('(...args: any[]) => void', '(...args: any[]) => void'))

    def test_typescripts_own_elision_is_not_a_rest_parameter(self):
        self.assertFalse(self.pattern('"a" | "b" | "c"', '"a" | "b" | ... 40 more ... | "c"'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-mutants --locked
    cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API of the core crate for SemVer breaks against the last published version. The version only
# moves in the release PR, so a break is accepted when a pending minor or major changeset covers the crate.
semver:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -uo pipefail
    if cargo semver-checks check-release -p caliper-docgen-core; then
        exit 0
    fi
    if grep -qsE '^cargo/caliper-docgen-core: (minor|major)$' .changeset/*.md; then
        echo "breaking API changes are covered by a pending minor or major changeset for caliper-docgen-core"
        exit 0
    fi
    echo "breaking API changes need a minor or major changeset for cargo/caliper-docgen-core" >&2
    exit 1

# Build with the minimum supported Rust version declared in Cargo.toml.
msrv:
    cargo +$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml) check --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test: test-rust test-ts

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:

1	# Parity with react-docgen-typescript
2	
3	`scripts/parity.py` measures Caliper against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) on five public repos with their dependencies installed, and `.github/workflows/parity.yml` runs it weekly and by hand. The scorecard (`docs/performance.md`) times source-only corpora; this measures what the docs say, on code whose imports resolve.
4	
5	## Corpora
6	
7	Each repo is fetched at a pinned commit and installed with its own package manager and lockfile, with lifecycle scripts off and every cache under `.parity/` (gitignored). Tests, stories, demos and `.d.ts` files are then removed from the source directory, so both tools read the same files. RDT parses every `.tsx` file in it as one program, rooted at the source directory.
8	
9	| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
12	| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
13	| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
14	| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
15	| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |
16	
17	A lockfile the pinned package manager rejects falls back to a fresh resolve; the install log says which ran.
18	
19	## What is measured
20	
21	Caliper runs in RDT's format with `--html-attributes full --include-unexported`, without (`--no-load-dependencies`, since dependency loading is on by default, ADR 0019) and with `--load-dependencies`; `scripts/parity.py` pins the flag for builds that know it. On components both tools report (same file, same name):
22	
23	| Measure | Meaning |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| Components matched | RDT's components with props that Caliper also reports |
26	| Non-React props reported | RDT's props not declared by `@types/react` that Caliper reports. Caliper lists React's DOM attributes as one inherited layer, as Storybook shows them |
27	| Same text | Identical type text after RDT's own normalization (`\| undefined` dropped) |
28	| Same or cosmetic | Also identical after dropping quotes, nested `\| undefined`, namespace prefixes, `Array<T>` spelling, a trailing `;`, outer parentheses and union order |
29	| Same control | Both types imply the same Storybook control (boolean, number, text, select, function, node, object) |
30	| Loss patterns | Shared props whose type carries less than RDT's, by pattern: a member read left as `X["k"]`, a lost rest parameter, an unbound type parameter, and so on. Two patterns count the reverse, where RDT carries less |
31	| Time and memory | Best of N wall time and peak RSS of `extract --json`, without and with `--load-dependencies`, next to RDT's own parse time |
32	
33	## Gates
34	
35	`--check` against `scripts/parity-baseline.json` fails when any rate above falls by more than 0.05 points, any of Caliper's loss patterns grows, or, with `--base-bin`, the build is more than 1.1× slower than the base on any corpus in either mode. The base is timed interleaved in the same job, so the runner's speed cancels out; the baseline's own times are a record of one machine, not a gate. Regenerate the baseline with a release build of main when a change is meant to move these numbers, and say so in the pull request.
36	
37	## Results, 2026-10-23
38	
39	`main` at `7bc120f4`, Apple Silicon laptop, 7 runs. With `--load-dependencies`:
40	
41	| Corpus | Components matched | Non-React props reported | Same text | Same or cosmetic | Same control | Caliper | RDT |
42	| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
43	| mantine | 331/389 | 99.7% | 48.0% | 50.9% | 93.1% | 55 ms, 109 MiB | 1.3 s, 458 MiB |
44	| chakra | 592/773 | 98.6% | 19.4% | 19.4% | 100.0% | 550 ms, 1,461 MiB | 24.8 s, 1,550 MiB |
45	| shadcn | 1519/1594 | 39.5% | 61.3% | 74.7% | 86.7% | 115 ms, 181 MiB | 4.0 s, 1,149 MiB |
46	| antd | 162/258 | 80.3% | 69.6% | 78.5% | 94.8% | 86 ms, 127 MiB | 2.4 s, 1,033 MiB |
47	| spectrum | 1087/1408 | 99.7% | 67.4% | 68.9% | 96.9% | 130 ms, 219 MiB | 2.2 s, 828 MiB |
48	
49	RDT's memory is its process's peak RSS; Caliper's time includes process start and RDT's excludes Node's. The full report, loss patterns included, is in `scripts/parity-baseline.json`.
50	
51	## TypeScript's checker as the oracle
52	
53	RDT is a second implementation with its own mistakes (on Spectrum it types `items` as its parent interface, `AriaMenuProps<T>`). `scripts/parity.py oracle` asks TypeScript 7.1's checker instead: `apps/validate/src/oracle.ts`, through the official `typescript/sync` client of `7.1.0-beta`, reads each prop's type for the components it finds the way RDT does, and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json` (with `--load-dependencies`). Both sides are reduced to kind, literal values, union members, object fields, function parameters (optional and rest included) and index signatures; the checker side also keeps the type's alias or declaring name. It is test-only: the semantic backend in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` is a separate, experimental opt-in.
54	
55	Each prop React's `@types/react` doesn't declare gets one verdict:
56	
57	| Verdict | Meaning |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| Identical | Both sides describe the same type |
60	| Spelled | The same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it (`StyleProp<MantineSpacing>`, `ReactNode`) |
61	| Less precise | Caliper's type is looser or left unevaluated: an opaque type, `string` for a literal union, a name the checker resolves further, an unbound parameter, a lost optional or rest marker, a missing field or index signature |
62	| Wrong | Caliper's type describes something else, such as a literal union missing members or `number` where csstype's `ZIndex` also allows strings |
63	| Checker any/error | The checker has no type: an error, `any`, or a top-level `unknown` where Caliper has one |
64	
65	A component's own type parameter that Caliper replaced with an instantiation (`multiple?: Multiple` with `Multiple extends boolean = false`, read as `false`) is "less precise" when Caliper's type is the parameter's default or its constraint, and "wrong" when it is neither; the checker side carries both. An optional prop of type `never` is the checker's `undefined`. `oracle.ts --dump FILE` (which `parity.py oracle` passes) writes every prop judged wrong or less precise, so two builds' verdicts can be diffed prop by prop; `apps/validate/src/oracle-compare.test.ts` holds the comparison's tests.
66	
67	Checker types are normalized once per type id and verdicts made once per pair, so Chakra's 470,878 shared props cost 1,241 comparisons. `--check` against `scripts/oracle-baseline.json` fails when identical-or-spelled falls, wrong rises, or components matched falls, by more than 0.05 points. The fixtures directory is a sixth corpus, read in place.

# Parity with react-docgen-typescript

`scripts/parity.py` measures Caliper against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) on five public repos with their dependencies installed, and `.github/workflows/parity.yml` runs it weekly and by hand. The scorecard (`docs/performance.md`) times source-only corpora; this measures what the docs say, on code whose imports resolve.

## Corpora

Each repo is fetched at a pinned commit and installed with its own package manager and lockfile, with lifecycle scripts off and every cache under `.parity/` (gitignored). Tests, stories, demos and `.d.ts` files are then removed from the source directory, so both tools read the same files. RDT parses every `.tsx` file in it as one program, rooted at the source directory.

| Corpus | Repository | Commit | Source directory | Install |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mantine | `mantinedev/mantine` | `e47e45af06427b3b2497100c2b849935c23af30d` | `packages/@mantine/core/src` | yarn, immutable |
| chakra | `chakra-ui/chakra-ui` | `fa9696f328ea5a0df8685c6d8460edbd779b63b9` | `packages/react/src` | pnpm, frozen |
| shadcn | `shadcn-ui/ui` | `ba1503c64472b82256d9de95e2e62c5901a38e8b` | `apps/v4` | pnpm, frozen |
| antd | `ant-design/ant-design` | `ba7ccbaa7b4b58ac1ff8e6fe2e78dfa10bfb5538` | `components` | npm, no lockfile (the repo commits none) |
| spectrum | `adobe/react-spectrum` | `797762ed3526ea12f089e321bd3891066affad70` | `packages` | yarn, immutable |

A lockfile the pinned package manager rejects falls back to a fresh resolve; the install log says which ran.

## What is measured

Caliper runs in RDT's format with `--html-attributes full --include-unexported`, without (`--no-load-dependencies`, since dependency loading is on by default, ADR 0019) and with `--load-dependencies`; `scripts/parity.py` pins the flag for builds that know it. On components both tools report (same file, same name):

| Measure | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Components matched | RDT's components with props that Caliper also reports |
| Non-React props reported | RDT's props not declared by `@types/react` that Caliper reports. Caliper lists React's DOM attributes as one inherited layer, as Storybook shows them |
| Same text | Identical type text after RDT's own normalization (`\| undefined` dropped) |
| Same or cosmetic | Also identical after dropping quotes, nested `\| undefined`, namespace prefixes, `Array<T>` spelling, a trailing `;`, outer parentheses and union order |
| Same control | Both types imply the same Storybook control (boolean, number, text, select, function, node, object) |
| Loss patterns | Shared props whose type carries less than RDT's, by pattern: a member read left as `X["k"]`, a lost rest parameter, an unbound type parameter, and so on. Two patterns count the reverse, where RDT carries less |
| Time and memory | Best of N wall time and peak RSS of `extract --json`, without and with `--load-dependencies`, next to RDT's own parse time |

## Gates

`--check` against `scripts/parity-baseline.json` fails when any rate above falls by more than 0.05 points, any of Caliper's loss patterns grows, or, with `--base-bin`, the build is more than 1.1× slower than the base on any corpus in either mode. The base is timed interleaved in the same job, so the runner's speed cancels out; the baseline's own times are a record of one machine, not a gate. Regenerate the baseline with a release build of main when a change is meant to move these numbers, and say so in the pull request.

## Results, 2026-10-23

`main` at `7bc120f4`, Apple Silicon laptop, 7 runs. With `--load-dependencies`:

| Corpus | Components matched | Non-React props reported | Same text | Same or cosmetic | Same control | Caliper | RDT |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| mantine | 331/389 | 99.7% | 48.0% | 50.9% | 93.1% | 55 ms, 109 MiB | 1.3 s, 458 MiB |
| chakra | 592/773 | 98.6% | 19.4% | 19.4% | 100.0% | 550 ms, 1,461 MiB | 24.8 s, 1,550 MiB |
| shadcn | 1519/1594 | 39.5% | 61.3% | 74.7% | 86.7% | 115 ms, 181 MiB | 4.0 s, 1,149 MiB |
| antd | 162/258 | 80.3% | 69.6% | 78.5% | 94.8% | 86 ms, 127 MiB | 2.4 s, 1,033 MiB |
| spectrum | 1087/1408 | 99.7% | 67.4% | 68.9% | 96.9% | 130 ms, 219 MiB | 2.2 s, 828 MiB |

RDT's memory is its process's peak RSS; Caliper's time includes process start and RDT's excludes Node's. The full report, loss patterns included, is in `scripts/parity-baseline.json`.

## TypeScript's checker as the oracle

RDT is a second implementation with its own mistakes (on Spectrum it types `items` as its parent interface, `AriaMenuProps<T>`). `scripts/parity.py oracle` asks TypeScript 7.1's checker instead: `apps/validate/src/oracle.ts`, through the official `typescript/sync` client of `7.1.0-beta`, reads each prop's type for the components it finds the way RDT does, and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json` (with `--load-dependencies`). Both sides are reduced to kind, literal values, union members, object fields, function parameters (optional and rest included) and index signatures; the checker side also keeps the type's alias or declaring name. It is test-only: the semantic backend in `docs/type-checker-integration.md` is a separate, experimental opt-in.

Each prop React's `@types/react` doesn't declare gets one verdict:

| Verdict | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Identical | Both sides describe the same type |
| Spelled | The same type, Caliper by name where the checker expands it (`StyleProp<MantineSpacing>`, `ReactNode`) |
| Less precise | Caliper's type is looser or left unevaluated: an opaque type, `string` for a literal union, a name the checker resolves further, an unbound parameter, a lost optional or rest marker, a missing field or index signature |
| Wrong | Caliper's type describes something else, such as a literal union missing members or `number` where csstype's `ZIndex` also allows strings |
| Checker any/error | The checker has no type: an error, `any`, or a top-level `unknown` where Caliper has one |

A component's own type parameter that Caliper replaced with an instantiation (`multiple?: Multiple` with `Multiple extends boolean = false`, read as `false`) is "less precise" when Caliper's type is the parameter's default or its constraint, and "wrong" when it is neither; the checker side carries both. An optional prop of type `never` is the checker's `undefined`. `oracle.ts --dump FILE` (which `parity.py oracle` passes) writes every prop judged wrong or less precise, so two builds' verdicts can be diffed prop by prop; `apps/validate/src/oracle-compare.test.ts` holds the comparison's tests.
